title: How Fast You Age During 40s May Predict Memory Lapses in Your 50s - Nautilus
gist: Penn State researchers measured biological aging in blood from 232 adults in their 40s and found that the pace of aging in midlife (via the DunedinPACE clock) can predict memory lapses a decade later.

insights.claim: The pace of biological aging during one's 40s can predict memory lapses roughly a decade later, according to a Penn State study.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Supports aging-clock diagnostics as early predictors for cognitive-decline interventions.
insights.quote: how quickly you age during midlife can predict memory lapses a decade later

insights.claim: The study used blood samples from 232 adults in their 40s during the 2000s, testing two molecular clocks for biological age and a third to measure aging rate.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Small sample size; treat as early evidence.
insights.quote: collected blood samples from 232 adults who were in their 40s during the 2000s

insights.claim: The DunedinPACE clock was built by tracking 19 organ-integrity biomarkers yearly in a cohort of 1,000 people since the 1970s.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: DunedinPACE is a credible pace-of-aging metric that longevity diagnostics firms can build on.
insights.quote: This clock, called DunedinPACE, was developed by following a cohort of 1,000 people beginning in the 1970s and tracking changes in 19 biomarkers
